title: Book 6 — Erato, Chapter 68
paragraphs: When his mother came, he placed some of the inner parts of the sacrificed animal in her hands and entreated her, saying: “Mother, I beg you, in the name of the other gods and above all of this Zeus, guardian of our household, to tell me the truth — who is really and truly my father? For Leotychides, in his quarrel with me, claimed that you came to Ariston already pregnant by your former husband. Others, repeating what is surely an empty tale, say that you went in to one of the servants, the keeper of the asses, and that I am his son. I therefore beseech you by the gods to tell me the truth. For if you did any of the things that are said of you, you did not do them alone — many other women have done the same. And the common report in Sparta is that there was no seed in Ariston capable of begetting children; for if there had been, his earlier wives would also have borne him children.”
